court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: IV Additional Principal Family Court at Chennai, O.P.Nos. 3212 of 2015, 1772 of 2017 and 986 of 2019
facts_of_case: The husband seeks dissolution of the marriage on grounds of cruelty, while the wife seeks restitution of conjugal rights. The husband also seeks custody of his minor children. The trial court decided in favor of the parties' respective claims.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to participate in the trial proceedings can result in their evidence being treated as no evidence.
legal_principles.held: Even though this Court posted as last chance and no further time for adducing evidence on respondent side, but respondent side no representation for several hearings. So on 09.12.2022, this Court recorded and it has been treated as no evidence on the respondent side.
cited_cases: D.Anitha vs D.Kesavan, (2026) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: A court may proceed with a case despite one party's failure to participate, as long as the other party is present and has filed their arguments.
legal_principles.held: Subsequently, the learned trial Judge had proceeded to deliver Judgment which is now the subject of this appeal.

outcome.final_order: The final order is not specified, but it appears that the appeals were allowed and the original orders were modified.
